OPERATOR SUBMITTED 1325 AND 1327 AT 23:51. THE FLIP IS MERGED ON gerrit/main AS 5892134975, BUT IT HAS NOT TAKEN EFFECT YET — autodeploy is DEFERRING it, which is bug 34cd's mechanism working exactly as designed:
    AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED {"reason": "review-in-flight", "detail": "target=58921349755b... in_flight=2 deferred_for=1259s bound=1800s"}
The running container is still the pre-cutover one (created 23:23:35Z), sets none of the three slots and no REBAR_USAGE_LOG, and resolves frontier/standard/trivial to anthropic:claude-opus-4-8 / -sonnet-4-6 / -haiku-4-5. So the bot is STILL ON ANTHROPIC as of this comment. When the 1800s bound expires autodeploy proceeds anyway and emits AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT — the marker whose alarm (rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts) I applied earlier today, so this will incidentally validate 34cd's alarm chain end-to-end on live traffic.

I INVESTIGATED WHETHER in_flight=2 WAS A LEAKED COUNTER, because it sat at exactly 2 for 21 minutes and a leaked counter would block EVERY deploy on this box, not just this one. IT IS REAL. In a 12-minute window: 11 LLM calls completed (code-review-base 131.0s and 178.1s, code-review-tests 74.4s, code-review-scope-intent 55.3s, code-review-api-compat 27.0s, code-review-verify 46.8s, code-review-docs 16.3s, and others), 2 votes cast, and SEVEN webhooks accepted. The gate is continuously busy because sessions are working in parallel, so in_flight rarely reaches 0. The deferral is correct behaviour and there is no defect here.

A MEASUREMENT TRAP WORTH RECORDING, because it produced a reading that looked like proof of a bug. Calling voter.in_flight_reviews() via 'docker compose exec' returns 0 while /health simultaneously reports 2. That is NOT /health lying: the counter is module-level state in the SERVER process, and 'docker compose exec' starts a FRESH python process with its own module namespace, so it reads its own zero. The same class of error as reading an env var on the HOST and attributing it to the container, which I also did earlier today. Only /health, served BY the server process, is a valid reading of in_flight.

TWO HONEST CONSEQUENCES OF THE SUBMIT ORDER, stated rather than smoothed over.

1. THE ORDERING CRITERION'S ITEM (c) WAS NOT COMPLETED BEFORE THE FLIP LANDED. Items (a) the runbook kill-switch entry, (b) the Bedrock client-error alarm — declared, APPLIED, and observed transitioning INSUFFICIENT_DATA -> OK on real data — and (d) the in-container provider import were all done and recorded BEFORE the merge. Item (c), the induced VOTER_ERROR with an observed rebar-gerrit-voter-errors OK -> ALARM transition, was still queued behind an idle window that the parallel-session load makes unlikely. REMEDY: execute the kill switch first (which is itself an acceptance criterion), which returns the bot to the Anthropic path, run the drill THERE, then re-apply the cutover. That satisfies (c)'s substance — an induced VOTER_ERROR observed while the bot is on the Anthropic path — and it proves the kill switch end-to-end at the same time, which is a stronger demonstration than the original sequence. But it will have been performed AFTER the flip rather than before, and that is a deviation from the criterion as written, not a reinterpretation of it.

2. 1325 MERGING COST ME THE PRE/POST COMPARISON FIXTURE. I had deliberately held it open so the SAME REVISION could be re-reviewed after the cutover; a merged change cannot be /rerun (Gerrit answers 409 'change is closed', which per bug c943 deliberately emits no VOTER_ERROR either). Findings A is banked and unaffected — 1325 @ a46d856c72, 0 blocking / 0 advisory / 0 dropped, provider_provenance provider='anthropic' — but findings B on that identical revision is now unobtainable. I will satisfy the criterion's SUBSTANCE ('no new blocking finding that is an artifact of the provider') against post-cutover reviews of real changes, comparing to the THREE pre-cutover Anthropic baselines I recorded today (1325, 1326 and 1327 artifacts, all 0 blocking), and I will state plainly that it is not the byte-identical same-revision comparison the criterion asks for. This also sits inside the operator's standing ruling that cross-model verdict comparison is informational rather than a gate.
